subject: A question about the students' ability comparison among factors

messages.author: affab363cb35318d
messages.subject: A question about the students' ability comparison among factors
parts:
Hello everybody

I'm using mirt to estimate students' abillity in mathematics assessment.  I use Rasch model, and there are 3 factors(dimmesions) for all items. The following is my code:

library(mirt)
cmodel <- mirt.model(' F1 = 1,2,,9,13,25,31,35
+     F2 = 3,4,,5,,6,10,11,14,15,16,17,18,19,21,22,26,27,28,29,33,34,36,37
+     F3 = 7,8,12,20,23,24,30,32,38')
cmod <- mirt(res, cmodel)
# Iteration: 38, Log-Lik: -295725.121, Max-Change: #0.00010                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
ab_3dim_rasch <- fscores(cmod)

Then I can get 3 theta values for each obj (student) in ab_3dim_rasch. 
F1 F2 F3
1 1.052343 2.150286 2.425081
2 1.052343 0.831582 1.111325
3 0.231678 0.823915 0.603081
4 0.385443 1.665016 0.524183
5 1.052343 1.590955 1.121802

My qustion is: for obj1, since 1.052343<2.150286, can I say obj1 has a higher grade in F2 than in F1? I guess the answer is no, because I find that the values on each factor fit N(0,sigma).
I have used the software Conquest and R package TAM, I can use command "constraints = cases" to set the mean of each latent dimension to zero, and if I don't want a 0 mean, I can write ""constraints = items".( If I understand correctly).  Is there a similiar argument for mirt? I have checked the package pdf but failed to find. Or do you know is there other packges or softwares that can work?

Thanks so much,
Wang Ziming

On Thu, Jun 15, 2017 at 12:55 AM, <238496...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello everybody

I'm using mirt to estimate students' abillity in mathematics assessment.  I use Rasch model, and there are 3 factors(dimmesions) for all items. The following is my code:

library(mirt)
cmodel <- mirt.model(' F1 = 1,2,,9,13,25,31,35
+     F2 = 3,4,,5,,6,10,11,14,15,16,17,18,19,21,22,26,27,28,29,33,34,36,37
+     F3 = 7,8,12,20,23,24,30,32,38')
cmod <- mirt(res, cmodel)
# Iteration: 38, Log-Lik: -295725.121, Max-Change: #0.00010
This is not a Rasch model. It's the graded response model (or 2PL if your data is dichotomous).

ab_3dim_rasch <- fscores(cmod)

Then I can get 3 theta values for each obj (student) in ab_3dim_rasch. 
F1 F2 F3
1 1.052343 2.150286 2.425081
2 1.052343 0.831582 1.111325
3 0.231678 0.823915 0.603081
4 0.385443 1.665016 0.524183
5 1.052343 1.590955 1.121802

My qustion is: for obj1, since 1.052343<2.150286, can I say obj1 has a higher grade in F1 than in F2? I guess the answer is no, because I find that the values on each factor fit N(0,sigma).

I don't know what the N(0, sigma) means in this context. Each of these observations has a different SE and VCOV matrix computed from their respective posterior distribution. While you could make the test you want, you would have to save the associated VCOV matrices and perform a Wald test directly for each observation. BUT, this is rather sub-optimal, because the VCOVs aren't truly unbiased because they require assuming the estimated IRT parameters are fixed and known with 100% certainty.

I have used the software Conquest and R package TAM, I can use command "constraints = cases" to set the mean of each latent dimension to zero, and if I don't want a 0 mean, I can write ""constraints = items".( If I understand correctly).  Is there a similiar argument for mirt? I have checked the package pdf but failed to find. Or do you know is there other packges or softwares that can work?

You could easily adjust the scale of the distribution to be exactly 0 for each column of factor scores, though I don't think that solves your problem or is at all interesting. What exactly are you trying to infer from your data? That will help us answer your questions better.

Phil

Thanks so much,
Wang Ziming

messages.author: f9b855547f00face
messages.subject: Re: A question about the students' ability comparison among factors
parts:
Here is the code use to estimate the RSM and to generate the Wright Map in 'mirt:'

mod1 <- mirt(resp, model=1, itemtype="rsm")
mod1
theta <- fscores(mod1, full.scores = TRUE, method = "ML")
hist(theta)
summary(mod1)
# Wright Map 
b <- sapply(1:ncol(resp), function(i) coef(mod1)[[i]][, "c"]) 
wrightMap(theta, b, item.side = itemClassic)


Attached to this you will find a screen shot of the plot generated. 


For comparison, here is the code used to generate the Wright Map in 'TAM:'

mod01 <- tam.mml(resp, constrain="persons", irtmodel="RSM", pid = dat_sub$ai_code_13, control=list(maxiter=1000, increment.factor=1.02))

xsi <- mod01$xsi
delta <- mod01$xsi
delta <- as.data.frame(delta[1:22, ])
ability <- tam.wle(mod01, WLE=FALSE)
wrightMap(ability$theta, delta$xsi, item.side = itemClassic)


Both ability estimates have been generated with ML.

messages.subject: Re: A question about the students' ability comparison among factors
parts:
Because mirt estimates models with the slope intercept format, not the classical IRT discrimination/difficulty parameterization (which is known to be unstable). So transforming b = -d/a is required, but since a = 1 for Rasch models then you just end up multiplying by -1. 

Phil

dichotomous). 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
ab_3dim_rasch <- fscores(cmod)

Then I can get 3 theta values for each obj (student) in ab_3dim_rasch. 
F1 F2 F3
1 1.052343 2.150286 2.425081
2 1.052343 0.831582 1.111325
3 0.231678 0.823915 0.603081
4 0.385443 1.665016 0.524183
5 1.052343 1.590955 1.121802

My qustion is: for obj1, since 1.052343<2.150286, can I say obj1 has a higher grade in F1 than in F2? I guess the answer is no, because I find that the values on each factor fit N(0,sigma).

I don't know what the N(0, sigma) means in this context. Each of these observations has a different SE and VCOV matrix computed from their respective posterior distribution. While you could make the test you want, you would have to save the associated VCOV matrices and perform a Wald test directly for each observation. BUT, this is rather sub-optimal, because the VCOVs aren't truly unbiased because they require assuming the estimated IRT parameters are fixed and known with 100% certainty. 

 
I have used the software Conquest and R package TAM, I can use command "constraints = cases" to set the mean of each latent dimension to zero, and if I don't want a 0 mean, I can write ""constraints = items".( If I understand correctly).  Is there a similiar argument for mirt? I have checked the package pdf but failed to find. Or do you know is there other packges or softwares that can work?

You could easily adjust the scale of the distribution to be exactly 0 for each column of factor scores, though I don't think that solves your problem or is at all interesting. What exactly are you trying to infer from your data? That will help us answer your questions better.

Phil
 

Thanks so much,
Wang Ziming

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: A question about the students' ability comparison among factors
parts:
In this script, if you passed coef(mod1, IRTpars = TRUE) then you'd obtain the transformed classical parameters. Likely this solves your problem.

Phil
On Wed, Aug 9, 2017 at 3:54 PM, B <brandon.f...@gmail.com> wrote:

Here is the code use to estimate the RSM and to generate the Wright Map in 'mirt:'

mod1 <- mirt(resp, model=1, itemtype="rsm")
mod1
theta <- fscores(mod1, full.scores = TRUE, method = "ML")
hist(theta)
summary(mod1)
# Wright Map 
b <- sapply(1:ncol(resp), function(i) coef(mod1)[[i]][, "c"]) 
wrightMap(theta, b, item.side = itemClassic)


Attached to this you will find a screen shot of the plot generated. 


For comparison, here is the code used to generate the Wright Map in 'TAM:'

mod01 <- tam.mml(resp, constrain="persons", irtmodel="RSM", pid = dat_sub$ai_code_13, control=list(maxiter=1000, increment.factor=1.02))

xsi <- mod01$xsi
delta <- mod01$xsi
delta <- as.data.frame(delta[1:22, ])
ability <- tam.wle(mod01, WLE=FALSE)
wrightMap(ability$theta, delta$xsi, item.side = itemClassic)


Both ability estimates have been generated with ML.
